newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernomyrdin says Russia budget income up.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin says Russia budget income up.

text.p: Russia's Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Wednesday budget income collection was much better in February than a year earlier and promised to reschedule arrears by indebted enterprises.
"The situation with incomes is not bad. For the first time we've hit the budgeted target," Chernomyrdin told the Federation Council upper house of parliament.
This would allow the government to pay 6.6 trillion roubles of wage arrears to teachers, he said.
He expected documents on rescheduling tax debts of 78 industrial enterprises with the biggest arrears to be signed soon by President Boris Yeltsin or the government.

Tax arrears totalled 70.5 trillion roubles in December. As of January 1 a total of 1,665 companies owed more than three billion roubles each to the budget. More than 80 owed more than 100 billion roubles each.

The International Monetary Fund has delayed a decision on whether to pay out money due in January or February from its $10 billion thre-year loan to Russia because it was concerned by the low level of tax revenues in January, and is seeking further information from the Russian authorities.
